document_summary: Berkeley Rent Board web page explaining the Annual General Adjustment (AGA), the annual rent increase ceiling under Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, including the 2026 AGA of 1.0%.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance Annual General Adjustment (AGA)
rules.requirement: Landlords of most fully covered units may raise rent annually only up to the AGA, set at 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U change, capped at 5%, with proper written notice. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%.
rules.key_value: 65% of Bay Area CPI-U, max 5%; 2026 AGA = 1.0%
rules.coverage_conditions: Most units fully covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance. No increase for the rest of the year the tenancy started and one additional calendar year. Notice: 30 days for increases of 10% or less, 90 days for more than 10%.
rules.exemptions: No AGA if registration fees are unpaid, a Rent Board order denies AGAs, there are serious repair problems or outstanding housing code violations, or interest on the security deposit is unpaid. Fixed-term leases wait until the term expires unless the lease allows the increase. Unused AGAs may be banked, and the 5% cap applies only to the AGA percentage.
rules.interaction: Government-owned or subsidized units must still go through the subsidizing agency's rent increase approval process. The cap was lowered from 7% to 5% by Measure BB.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance); Berkeley Rent Board Reg. 1148 (AGA 2026 Order)
rules.quoted_span: The AGA is set by taking 65% of the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers in the Bay Area from July 1 through June 30 of the prior year.
rules.extraction_notes: Agency summary page; the Measure BB change from 7% to 5% has no date stated on this page, so effective_date is null. The AGA is adjusted each year in October and takes effect on January 1 (2026 AGA 1.0%). The BMC chapter citation is inferred from the Rent Ordinance and is not given in this document.
